Add extra monthly or one-time payments and see your payoff date move up and interest saved. No signup.
- [Amortization, Explained: Where Your Payment Actually Goes](https://loanmath.website/guides/amortization-explained.html): Amortization is why your first mortgage payment is 86% interest. How the schedule really works, when principal finally takes over, and how to read any amortization table.
- [APR Calculator — True APR With Fees & Total Cost](https://loanmath.website/tools/apr-calculator.html): Free APR calculator: loan amount, stated rate, fees and term in — the true APR, the monthly payment and the total cost of the loan out. See what fees quietly do to the rate.
- [APR vs Interest Rate: What the Fees Do to the Truth](https://loanmath.website/guides/apr-vs-interest-rate.html): The interest rate prices the loan you asked for; the APR prices the cash you actually received. On a $10,000 loan, a single $500 fee turns a 10% rate into a 13.56% APR — here is the arithmetic, and how to shop with it.
- [Calculator.net Alternatives for Loans and Mortgages](https://loanmath.website/guides/calculator-net-alternatives-for-loans.html): Calculator.net is deep and deserves its reputation. For loan and mortgage questions specifically, here is the focused alternative: one solver for payment, amount, term or rate — nothing to sign up for.

- [Embed Our Calculators — Free, No Attribution Required](https://loanmath.website/embed.html): Put any Loan Math calculator on your own website free: pick a tool, copy one snippet, done. No attribution required, no sign-up, always up to date.
- [Extra Payments: The Cheapest Way to Shorten Any Loan](https://loanmath.website/guides/extra-payments-shorten-any-loan.html): Every extra dollar goes straight to principal — and on a $300,000 mortgage, $200 a month extra erases 81 payments and saves $91,173 of interest. The math of prepaying, done honestly.
- [How Student Loans Are Calculated: Interest Before You Ever Make a Payment](https://loanmath.website/guides/how-student-loans-are-calculated.html): Unsubsidized student loans start charging interest the day the money lands — and unpaid interest capitalizes into principal at graduation. On $20,000 borrowed over four years at 6.52%, you start repayment owing $23,479.57. Here is every step.
- [How to Calculate a Personal Loan Payment by Hand](https://loanmath.website/guides/calculate-personal-loan-payment-by-hand.html): One formula, five minutes: M = P x r(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1) worked digit by digit on a $10,000 loan at 10% — $322.67 a month — plus the fee adjustment lenders hope you skip and the zero-rate shortcut.
- [How to Calculate Your Car Loan Payment Before You Visit the Dealer](https://loanmath.website/guides/calculate-car-loan-payment-before-the-dealer.html): Walk in knowing the number: how to price a car loan yourself — amount financed after down payment and trade-in, the payment formula, and the term-stretch trick that makes a pricier car look cheaper.
- [How to Pay Off a Car Loan Early (and What It Actually Saves)](https://loanmath.website/guides/pay-off-car-loan-early.html): Extra payments on a car loan go straight to principal — but how much do they save? On a $28,000 loan at 6%, $100 a month extra ends the loan 10 months early and saves $810.45. The mechanics, the numbers, and the two checks to run first.
- [Loan Math — free online calculators](https://loanmath.website/): Loan Math explains how borrowing is actually computed: amortization, interest and APR mechanics worked out in the open — plus the full library of 154 free calculators. No signup, no lead forms.

The honest break-even method: compare total costs over the years you will actually stay, including the costs both sides hide.
- [Snowball vs Avalanche: What the Order Actually Costs](https://loanmath.website/guides/snowball-vs-avalanche-cost-difference.html): Both methods pay the same minimums on everything and attack one debt at a time — the only difference is which one. On a $15,500 stack of three debts, that choice is worth $359.21 and one month. The full race, priced.

- [What Is a HELOC? The Lender&#x27;s Side of a Home Equity Line](https://loanmath.website/guides/what-is-a-heloc.html): A HELOC is a revolving line that uses your house as collateral — which is why it is cheap and why it is dangerous. How lenders price it (prime plus a margin), what the payment is really made of, the fees and freeze clauses, and what it costs on $20,000.
